remarks.para: emits ten hand-written series and nothing else, so the 81 Metrics.Create* declarations across PrometheusMetrics, WriteAheadLog, and the Lean integration types were declared, incremented at runtime, and never scraped. Alerts and dashboards naming them could not fire regardless of system state.

Two things make appending the registry correct rather than merely additive. First, the snapshot-backed instruments are refreshed here, on the scrape: PrometheusMetricsUpdater is constructed only by tests, so nothing in the host ever called UpdateFromSnapshot and every gauge it feeds sat at its initial zero — served but never written, which reads identically to a healthy system. Collect-on-scrape makes the values current exactly when they are read and needs no background timer or lifecycle. member.summary: High-throughput, backpressured pipeline that decouples producers from storage sinks. Includes periodic flushing, capacity monitoring, performance metrics, and optional Write-Ahead Log (WAL) integration for crash-safe durability.

member.name: T:Meridian.Application.Reconciliation.RetainedInternalReconciliationPopulationProvider
member.summary: Resolves the internal book (positions and cash) a statement run reconciles against from Meridian's own retained account records, replacing the fail-closed empty default so shipped imports actually reconcile instead of surfacing every external row as an unmatched break. Lives in the application layer so both the browser workstation service graph and the CLI command graph resolve the same retained-book provider over shared account and position stores.
member.remarks:
Sources and assumptions (documented for operator/domain review):
Cash is read from the account's retained balance timeline as of the statement period end () — the most recent internal balance at or before the period close, not the account's newest balance, so a closed statement is never reconciled against a balance recorded after the period.
Positions are read best-effort from the retained position snapshot effective at or before the statement period end, selected from snapshot history (see ResolvePeriodSnapshotAsync) so a later snapshot never displaces the period-appropriate book; market value is left unspecified so the engine matches on quantity and account/security identity. Known limitation: this reads the legacy unowned snapshot partition via the two-argument and history overloads. Snapshots written through the owner-scoped accounting-capture path (tenant/company/fund/book/entity) are invisible here and fail closed to position breaks until an appropriately authorized owner-scoped query seam is resolved for the account.
The statement run's FundAccountId must be a Meridian fund-account GUID; an operator label that is not a GUID resolves no internal book, and every row fails closed to a break.
Internal records are labeled with the run's external (custodian) account key — the same key the statement side normalizes to — so a statement row reconciles against Meridian's book for the account under reconciliation regardless of the per-row account string the custodian emits.
Ledger-transaction population is intentionally left empty (fail closed to breaks). Sourcing it is a domain decision, not a wiring gap: the reconciliation context carries no ledger-book/period scope key, the ledger journal is double-entry (each entry has several GL lines, so projecting a single custodian-visible movement — its net amount, quantity, security, external id, and type — is a modeling choice), only custodian-reconcilable postings should be projected (accruals, revaluations, and inter-book transfers never appear on a statement), and fund-scoped journal reads are tenant-authorized. Populating it wrongly would fabricate false matches or flood false internal-only breaks, both worse than the current fail-closed behavior, so it awaits an authorized period-scoped ledger source and an agreed journal→transaction projection.
Every resolution failure degrades to so the matcher never fabricates a match and the import workflow never throws.

member.summary:
Resolves the durable accounting ledger books a published Security Master revision could have touched, so the period-aware restatement resolver (Phase 3) can route each book by its accounting period lock status. This is the publish-time feed for ; without it the resolver is a no-op end-to-end (an empty affected-book set short-circuits to no restatement).
Restatement protects durable accounting books — the only ledger surface that carries an accounting-period lock. Those books are keyed by fund profile, so a fund-scoped impact resolves to that fund's books. When the impact reports no ledger exposure, or no durable ledger backend is configured, there is no locked book to protect and the affected set is empty.

member.name: T:Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.LedgerBookAffectedResolver
member.summary: Default over . When the impact reports ledger exposure for a known fund profile, every durable ledger book registered for that fund is treated as potentially affected and routed through the period-aware lock check.

remarks.para: The is an optional dependency (registered only when a durable ledger backend is configured — see LedgerFeatureRegistration, which binds the store via GetService). With no store, no durable book carries a period lock, so the affected set is empty.

Granularity: the display-oriented does not carry per-book identifiers, so resolution is at fund-book granularity — conservative by design, since over-including a fund's books yields an extra restatement proposal (operator-reviewed, never auto-applied) whereas under-including would risk a silent mutation of a closed book. Narrowing to the specific posting books that referenced the security (via journal-line dimensions) and cross-fund expansion for unscoped impacts are deferred to later slices.

Phase 2 governed write surface for the Security Master Passport Workbench.
UpdateSecurityFieldAsync — justification-gated operator field edits staged as overlay annotations in . The passport-displayed security version is an optimistic-concurrency staleness guard (a stale ExpectedVersion surfaces as → HTTP 409). Overlay edits are deliberately NOT appended to the economic event stream: that stream is replayed verbatim to rebuild the passport, so a partial field-edit payload would corrupt the economic definition.
ResolveSourceConflictAsync — scored by the conflict-authority policy, enforces acknowledged deviation, and closes the underlying conflict via with an atomic open→resolved transition; a concurrent duplicate resolution surfaces as rather than silently overwriting the first operator's winner.
SubmitForApprovalAsync / ApproveRevisionAsync — route through the approval gate and advance the durable lifecycle (Draft → Submitted → Approved) with compare-and-set transitions.
PublishRevisionAsync — refuses to publish unless the revision is durably Approved, fans out to the ordered seam (Phase 3 supplies handlers), and surfaces any handler failure () leaving the revision Approved for an idempotent retry; only an all-success fan-out transitions the revision to Published.
